subject: Maximum number of files to run?

messages.author: a7ac0f2eab029bc7
messages.subject: Maximum number of files to run?
parts:
Hello, 

I am running GGIR on a study that contains 835 gt3x files and am having trouble. Mainly, I am running into an error of "cannot allocate vector of size XX Mb" A previous conversation in this group suggests that computer memory may be an issue, but my computer has 16 GB of memory. 

This code runs well when tested on a random sample of 100 participants, so I am wondering if there is a limit to how many gt3x files GGIR can process at a time? Or if this is an issue with my computer?

Thank you, 

Reagan

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: Maximum number of files to run?
parts:
There isn't a limit as with do.parallel=T it will run ncores-1 files at a time e.g. if you have 8 cores it will process 7 files at once and I believe it's recommended to have ~2gb per file in parallel. You could use the maxNcores and try a lower number if you find your PC is struggling to run at the default max number of cores. If that's not helping then someone else may need to chip in with a suggestion or I would be just suggesting that you run 100 files at once e.g. f0=1 and f1=100, then re-run with f0=101 and f1=200 etc. until you have them all if you are looking for a (potentially) quick workaround to get things processing.

An alternate thing to look at would be tools>memory inside R in case there is some bottleneck there and you just need to increase the allocation to your R session. 

Thanks,
Ben

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Maximum number of files to run?
parts:
Could it be that you have one or more very large files, which are no part of your test run with 100 files? I have had that issue with some ActiGraph gt3x files which had a lot of sporadic idle sleep mode periods, which can eat a lot of memory.

In that case I recommend:
  • Move the largest files out of your data folder
  • Process all your data as you normally do
  • Move the largest files back
  • Set do.parallel = FALSE and overwrite = FALSE
  • Run your R script again, this should then only process the large files.

Another issue I had in the past was that memory per core ratio was too low, which I fixed by installing extra memory in my machine. 

Best,

Vincent
